title: The Onyx Club and the reputation of Froeberg
summary: Duerr remembers lines at the Onyx Club, Froeberg with the Ink Spots, and Froeberg's standing and later career.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Yeah, I knew him too. I knew all those guys pretty well. I used to go around the honors club and they worked there. There used to be a line outside, a half a block long trying to get in the honors club. And then Frober worked at the honors club later on. And when they got out of there they used to piano alone for a while. And they had the ink spots too in there for a while and Frober played piano and the ink spots played in between or something like that. He worked there for a good time. He'd go around there and hang
around there. What did people think of Frober?

Was he a big name? He was a big name around New York. He could have got much further than he, although he did all right I guess, but I mean he got to be pretty well known around New York school, I tell you. He was a good piano player at that time. When we used to go up to Harlem there used to be a lot of guys who would go up to hear him play, I tell you that. Johnny Green used to go up and listen to him play. And a lot of other piano players, Eddie Bushkin used to go up and listen to him all the time and cook. They were a little smarter than Frober because they made it more. I mean they didn't get the money more. Frober's doing all right now in Florida. Yeah, well somebody said he's not playing too much in Florida. I don't know. Somebody was a little older, I don't know. But he was going to Nassau and wasn't it? Oh yeah, he was going to Nassau too and he had to make pretty good money. I know the last time I had
it. What about when he was with Goodman? Was Goodman making any money there?
Well, he didn't make money. You know at that time I thought of it as a deal was. I don't know exactly what it was. I guess it was good for that time. He didn't stay with Goodman too
long. What about Sterling Bowes? He was a good one.
Yeah, Sterling Bowes. He doesn't mean that I don't hear them for years and you just don't get them again. Didn't Clark Randall have a name? What was the name?

No, I'm trying to think of these guys' names. Somebody, Joe Roden or somebody. Joe Roden? Well, Ben Pollock's band broke up and somebody had it for a while. I can't remember who had it. But before they went to the Bobcats band.
